_units: abv %vol; sugar g per 100 ml (solids: % by mass); acid % titratable; dash = 0.8 ml; drop = 0.05 ml
_rules: Vetoes are medical: classify on the safe side (Robin 2026-09-24)
nutmeg, coconut, orgeat, amaretto, hazelnut liqueur, pine nuts -> nuts
undistilled beer/malt -> gluten; distilled grain spirits are NOT gluten
spice = heat only (bitters and baking spices are not spice)
wine fining agents ignored unless a named bottle is labelled

unknown ingredient -> the Mixologist adds it with scripts/add_ingredient.py, allergens on the safe side (every veto it could plausibly touch). His call, not Robin's: the guest's own veto protects them. The table follows the drink, never limits it (Robin 2026-09-25)

sugar.source: pure sucrose; dissolved volume 0.63 ml per g (density 1.59)

sugar_cube.name: sugar cube
sugar_cube.source: ~4 g per cube; dissolved volume 0.63 ml per g

nutmeg.why: Robin 2026-09-24: nutmeg counts as nuts, to be safe

orgeat.source: Liquid Intelligence, ingredient table (pdf 140-141, pp. 136-137): any nut orgeat

egg_white.name: egg white
egg_white.source: ~30 ml per large egg white (LI egg-white drinks)

tequila_reposado.name: tequila reposado
tequila_reposado.source: Liquid Intelligence pdf 140 note: straight spirits = label ABV, no sugar, minimal acid (40% typical)

agave_nectar.name: agave nectar (straight)
agave_nectar.source: Liquid Intelligence p. 53: ~75% sugar by weight, dense; use ~60% of the simple-syrup volume, so ~100 g/100 ml sucrose-equivalent. Fructose tastes sweeter cold (p. 51)

lemongrass_syrup.name: lemongrass syrup (1:1)
lemongrass_syrup.source: 1:1 sugar syrup infused with lemongrass: sugar as LI simple syrup (pp. 136-137); lemongrass adds aroma only (Flavor Matrix pdf 164)

salt.name: kosher salt (for half the rim)
salt.source: plain sodium chloride; rimmed on the outside of half the glass (Codex p. 212 method), not modelled in balance

vanilla_syrup.name: vanilla syrup (1:1)
vanilla_syrup.source: 1:1 sugar syrup steeped with a split vanilla pod: sugar as LI simple syrup (pp. 136-137); vanilla adds aroma only

cherry_tomato.name: ripe cherry tomatoes, muddled and strained (juice)
cherry_tomato.source: unsourced standard value (ripe tomato ~3-4 g sugars/100 g, ~0.35-0.5% titratable acid as citric); no tomato row in LI's table (pp. 136-137)

tomato_vanilla_syrup.name: cherry-tomato and vanilla syrup (1:1 by weight, tomato juice and sugar)
tomato_vanilla_syrup.source: derived: 100 g strained ripe cherry-tomato juice (cherry_tomato row, unsourced standard value) + 100 g sugar ~ 162 ml (LI simple-syrup density, pp. 136-137) -> 63.9 g sugar/100 ml, 0.28% acid; vanilla pod adds aroma only

creme_de_noyaux.name: crème de noyaux (apricot-kernel liqueur)
creme_de_noyaux.source: unsourced standard value (~30% ABV, sugar assumed like maraschino, LI pp. 136-137); made from apricot/peach kernels, almond-flavoured: nuts on the safe side, same call as amaretto/maraschino

egg_yolk.name: egg yolk (one large, raw)
egg_yolk.source: unsourced standard value (~17 ml per large yolk, negligible sugar/acid); raw egg: the veto enum's only egg entry is 'egg-white', so a yolk counts there on the safe side

cherry_tomato_whole.name: cherry tomato (whole, garnish)
cherry_tomato_whole.source: garnish only: one small ripe cherry tomato, slit and sat on the rim; not in the balance

cranberry_syrup.name: cranberry syrup (1:1 by weight, unsweetened 100% cranberry juice and sugar, stirred cold)
cranberry_syrup.source: derived: 100 g unsweetened 100% cranberry juice (unsourced standard value: ~4 g sugars/100 g, ~2.4% titratable acid as citric) + 100 g sugar ~ 162 ml (LI simple-syrup density, pp. 136-137) -> 64.2 g sugar/100 ml, 1.48% acid. Not cranberry cocktail (Codex p. 183)

caramel_shard.name: dark caramel shard (sugar cooked dry to dark amber, set thin on baking paper, broken)
caramel_shard.source: derived: sucrose cooked to dark amber, modelled as sucrose by mass; caramelised sugar tastes less sweet than sucrose (Liquid Intelligence pdf 187) and loses a little mass in cooking, so the printed sugar overstates the sweetness a guest tastes

absinthe_lucid.name: Lucid Absinthe Supérieure (62%)
absinthe_lucid.source: label: 62% ABV (124 US proof), grande wormwood, fennel, sweet anise; Hester, fact card ted-breaux-absinthe F15 (Wikipedia citing the 2007 label approval + a specialist retailer). Unsweetened, as absinthe verte

tamarind_water.name: tamarind water (100 g sour seedless tamarind pulp block soaked in 250 ml hot water, pressed through a sieve)
tamarind_water.source: Hester's tamarind fact card (El-Siddig et al. 2006, secondary): dried pulp 8-18% tartaric (about half bound as cream of tartar, not sour) and 25-45% sugars; at 100 g : 250 ml, total acid 2.3-5.1%, sour part ~half; sugar 7-13 g/100. F5: a 20-24% pulp drink syrup ~1.11% total acidity. Row uses the middle of the sour range (2.0%) and of sugar (10). Sour block only (sweet Thai 2-3%). Revised by Tomás round 4 (was 20 g / 4.0%, an overestimate).

vodka_citrus.name: citrus vodka (lemon-flavoured, unsweetened, e.g. Absolut Citron style)
vodka_citrus.source: unsourced standard value: flavoured vodkas of the Citron style are bottled at 40% and read as unsweetened; if a bottle is sweetened, sugar is understated

cranberry_juice_unsweetened.name: unsweetened 100% cranberry juice (bottled, 'just cranberry')
cranberry_juice_unsweetened.source: unsourced standard value (same basis as cranberry_syrup's juice: ~4 g sugars/100 g, ~2.4% titratable acid as citric). Codex p. 183: 'very tannic'

cranberry_cocktail.name: cranberry juice cocktail (sweetened, ~27% juice)
cranberry_cocktail.source: unsourced estimate: ~30 g sugars per 240 ml label serving; acid = 27% of unsweetened juice's 2.4%. For the 'before' comparison only

rum_aged_tea.name: aged rum steeped with black tea (about 30 g loose black tea per litre, 20-40 minutes, strained)
rum_aged_tea.source: method after LI p. 268-269 (Arnold's tea vodka: 32 g tea per 1 L, 20-40 min, 'go dark'); tea adds no measurable sugar or acid; a little rum is lost in the leaves, ABV change ignored

basil_leaf.name: fresh basil leaf (sweet/Genovese basil)
basil_leaf.source: herb leaf, shaken with the drink for aroma and fine-strained out; not modelled in balance. Pairing: Flavor Matrix, Berry (pdf 52: basil a surprise pairing for berries incl. cranberry) and Kiwi (pdf 156: basil and vaccinium both surprise pairings)

green_olive_brine.name: green olive brine (from plain, unstuffed green olives in brine)
green_olive_brine.source: unsourced standard value: brine of salt, water and a little lactic acid/vinegar; salt ~8% not modelled; dosed by the dash as a seasoning

passion_fruit_syrup.name: passion fruit syrup (1:1 by weight, fresh or bottled juice and sugar)
passion_fruit_syrup.source: unsourced standard value: 1:1 juice:sugar by weight; passion fruit juice ~3.5% acid (citric), halved; sugar as a 1:1 syrup

lime_caraway_cordial.name: lime and caraway cordial (150 ml fresh lime juice, 150 g sugar, zest of 4 limes, 1 tsp caraway seeds; warmed to dissolve, never boiled, steeped 20 min, strained)
lime_caraway_cordial.source: computed from its recipe with LI table values (lime juice 1.6 g sugar / 6.0% acid; sugar 0.62 ml per g dissolved): 152.4 g sugar and 9 g acid in ~243 ml; zest and seeds carry aroma only; unsourced for heat losses
